text: Next morning, the guild mourns him for the press. Mok praises him for exactly what he was paid to do.
Hand on heart, Mok plays the grieving leader. Last night he shut the door on him.
On the steps outside, Yoo Bomi, twenty-one, E-rank ranger and BomBom TV streamer, works her drone like she owns the street.
To her, a dead trap-tester is content, and her chat barely knows who he was.
Right past her walks the trap rat himself, bandaged, with Yerin and a small masked husk behind him.
Bomi's head whips round, and her drone swings after it.
She bounces into his path: the dead guy, live on her stream. Jaeha finds the sky very interesting.
Behind him, the husk is deeply unimpressed.
Jaeha bows politely and steps round her. He has an appointment.
The doors at the back of the hall swing open, and every head turns.
Yerin half hides behind his shoulder as the whole room stares.
At the podium, Mok freezes mid-word. Dead men aren't supposed to walk in.
Jaeha walks up the aisle, apologising for being late. In front of these cameras, polite is a weapon.
Then he stands beside his own memorial portrait and politely asks for the floor.
The room explodes. Bomi's stream jumps to almost ten thousand, and the chat can't decide: resurrection or stunt?
Mok recovers fast and crushes him in a bear hug for the cameras, all teeth and no warmth.
Through a smile that never moves, he gives Jaeha an order only he can hear.
In a back office: Mok, the two hunters who got out with him, and Nib by the door like furniture.
Mok slides over a fat envelope and a confession: ten million won to sign his name to Mok's version.
Jaeha thanks him sweetly and asks for a day to think. He's stalling.
Because the phone in his chest pocket is recording every word.
The smile drops. Mok barely hides the threat: next time, Jaeha might not come out of a gate.
The crossbow hunter turns a little brass compass in her fingers, studying the husk with far too much interest.
Then Mok turns on Yerin. Her offer is cheaper: back his story, or lose her job.
Her eyes go from fear to something harder.
She slaps her contract card down on his lie. She saw who shut that door, and she's done. Even Jaeha blinks.
On his way out, the husk stops in the doorway and breaks character for one line.
Mok goes slack with shock. Behind him, the crossbow hunter slowly smiles.
Alone, Mok crushes the statement in his fist. Nobody took the money.
Down the corridor, Black Hound hunters step aside, one dropping his cup. Yerin's chin is up.
By sunset they're home: one small room on a rooftop, laundry lines, and the river for a view.
Waiting in the doorway: Kang Seoa, fifteen, his sister, who runs the household budget. Crying and furious at once.
She pounds his chest, and he lets her. He broke his promise, then went to his own memorial before coming home.
Then he pulls her into a hug and rests his chin on her head.
On the door behind them, the rent notice is still taped up, red stamp and all.
Then, mid-sniffle, Seoa notices that her brother has brought guests.
Yerin bows far too low and leads with the worst possible fact. Jaeha tries the husk story again.
Seoa turns the laptop round: three hundred thousand won due, nothing saved. Last night, Jaeha turned down four hundred million.
Dinner is instant ramen with an egg in it. Nib's fingers hover over a bowl, and stop.
He nudges the bowl toward Jaeha with one fingertip. Same rule as the coffee.
Seoa's chopsticks stop halfway to her mouth. Husks don't eat either.
Mouth full of noodles, Nib drops the act entirely. Jaeha hides his face.
Seoa and Yerin cling to each other while he slurps.
Then Jaeha stands up proudly to show off his trophy. He has learned nothing from last night.
The Ninth Wall Blade drops out of the air and punches through the floor. The ramen bowls jump.
Jaeha ends up flat on his face. Nib, still holding his ramen, offers a review. Jaeha doesn't argue.
Seoa's glasses flash white. Somewhere in her head, the budget just got worse.
Later that night, Jaeha leans alone on the railing, looking out over the river.
He turns the chain link in his bandaged fingers. The knight went home. Whoever chained him is still out there.
And on his phone, the recording from the back room.
Nib joins him on the railing with his ramen, bare feet dangling. He has opinions about Seoa. So does Jaeha.
Nib looks into his bowl, and his mouth nearly softens. From him, this is high praise.
Across the city stands Kanghan Tower, sixty storeys of black glass. Someone up there is working late.
A man with a cane reads the report. Someone left Gate 0912's core behind, and the signal has a name: Operator protocol.
Four faces on four screens: Mok, his shield-bearer, Yerin, and Jaeha.
And one signal spike, far above the rest.
In the dark glass, only silver glasses and a polite smile show. Four survivors, and one should not have survived.
His hand tightens on the cane, a violet core glowing under his fingers. The hunt for the Operator begins.
